name: The obstacle becomes a furtherance
originalThought: QUELLE (Long 1862, 5.20): 'the mind ... changes every hindrance ... into an aid ...'. NOTE: do NOT quote the Hays wording ('what stands in the way becomes the way'), which is copyrighted.
softwareInterpretation: INTERPRETATION: Errors/exceptions are information, not a nuisance to be suppressed. Appropriate error handling makes the obstacle usable.
preconditions: Presence of error-handling constructs (catch clauses, promises, error-returning calls).
limits: Legitimate empty handling exists (expected cache miss); comment/heuristic signals needed; not every language has checked exceptions.
counterexamples: A catch with deliberate, commented handling ('optional cache miss expected, intentionally ignored').
A catch with logging or a fallback.
